categories.name: Protein
categories.context: Protein powders are compared on price per 100 g of protein, not per tub: pack size, protein percentage and shipping decide the real cost.

categories.name: Creatine
categories.context: Creatine monohydrate is chemically the same across brands, so cost per 5 g serving and third-party testing are the differentiators.

categories.name: Amino acids
categories.context: EAA and BCAA products differ mostly in free-form dose per serving; compare grams of actives, not scoop size.

categories.name: Pre-workout
categories.context: Pre-workouts vary by caffeine load and whether the label is fully disclosed. Several markets require warnings above a caffeine threshold.

categories.name: Recovery & sleep
categories.context: Recovery and sleep products are single-ingredient or small blends; the regulatory status of some actives differs by market.

categories.name: Vitamins & minerals
categories.context: Micronutrients are compared on form (chelated vs oxide), dose per capsule and cost per day.

categories.name: Gainers & carbs
categories.context: Gainers and carbohydrate mixes are bulk goods where shipping is often the deciding cost.

categories.name: Metabolism
categories.context: Metabolism products contain the most market-restricted actives in this catalogue; availability varies per country.

categories.name: Health & immunity
categories.context: General health products with long shelf life, frequently bought as add-ons to reach free shipping thresholds.

articles.title: What protein really costs: price per 100 g of protein across 12 countries
articles.author: Comparo Editorial
articles.excerpt: We normalised 640 offers to a single metric — price per 100 g of protein, shipping included. The gap between the cheapest and most expensive market is 41 %.
body: We normalised 640 offers to a single metric — price per 100 g of protein, shipping included. The gap between the cheapest and most expensive market is 41 %.

The method is deliberately simple. We take offers from verified merchants that genuinely deliver to the selected country on the day of measurement and normalise them to a single metric including shipping. Offers with no stated availability or no shipping cost are excluded from the calculation.

The result shows that the deciding line item is often not the product price itself but the combination of shipping, the free shipping threshold and any active coupon. A shopper comparing product price alone pays roughly 12 % more on average.

The underlying data lives in the comparison engine and refreshes several times a day from merchant product feeds. Every product carries a price history chart, and you can set an alert on a target price.

guides.title: How to compare supplement shops in Germany
guides.excerpt: A practical checklist: delivery cost to your postcode, free shipping threshold, return window, support response time and whether the shop publishes its carrier.
body: A practical checklist: delivery cost to your postcode, free shipping threshold, return window, support response time and whether the shop publishes its carrier.

The method below is deliberately boring. Every step uses data you can see on the platform: the offer table, the shipping row, the rating breakdown and the price chart. Nothing depends on trusting a single number.
Start by fixing your delivery country, because everything downstream changes with it: which shops are even eligible, what shipping costs, and whether the product is purchasable in your market at all.

Then normalise. Compare totals including shipping, and per unit where the pack sizes differ. A listing that looks 15 % cheaper is regularly more expensive once the pack size and delivery are accounted for.

Finally, weigh reliability. A two-euro saving at a shop with a 40 % complaint resolution rate is not a saving. Response rate and resolution rate are published on every shop profile for exactly this reason.

xpSources.label: Price correction
xpSources.why: A feed price that no longer matches the shop page. Confirmed against the shop within the hour.
xpSources.proof: Screenshot or the shop URL; moderation re-checks the page.

xpSources.label: Stock correction
xpSources.why: An offer listed in stock that is not. Stock confidence is otherwise guessed from feed freshness alone.
xpSources.proof: Shop page state at the time of the report.

xpSources.label: Coupon outcome
xpSources.why: Whether a code actually applied, on which basket, in which market. The single most perishable fact we hold.

xpSources.label: Delivery report
xpSources.why: Order date, dispatch, arrival and carrier. This is what makes a delivery median real rather than modelled.
xpSources.proof: Order confirmation date and the parcel arrival date.

xpSources.label: Label photograph
xpSources.why: The amount-per-serving panel, readable. Dosing is the comparison nobody else in this category can do.
xpSources.proof: Photo of the panel with the lot number visible.
xpSources.collects: Dosing, price per gram of active

xpSources.label: Dosing correction
xpSources.why: A declared amount that differs from the tub. Highest-value correction we accept.
xpSources.proof: Label photo plus the field being corrected.

verdicts.question: Which whey isolate is the best value per 100 g of protein in DE?
verdicts.method: Two weeks of argument in the Comparisons section, then a ranked vote. Our data team published the price-per-gram table beforehand and did not vote.
verdicts.answer: Whey Isolate 90 at the pack size above 1 kg. The clear-whey options lost on protein per serving once the maths was done per 100 g rather than per scoop.
verdicts.dissent: 18 % preferred Clear Whey Refresh on taste and said the premium was worth it — recorded rather than averaged away.

verdicts.question: Is creatine HCl worth the premium over monohydrate?
verdicts.method: Evidence thread with three verified experts, then a ranked vote. Brand accounts were allowed to post and were labelled.
verdicts.answer: No, for the stated reason: the price per gram of creatine is three to ten times higher and the community could not point to a study showing a practical difference.
verdicts.dissent: 11 % reported better tolerance on HCl. Kept, because tolerance is exactly the kind of thing an average hides.

verdicts.question: Which shops quote a landed total that turns out to be true?
verdicts.method: Members submit an order confirmation and the quoted total; our team reconciles against the order record. Vote opens when 200 reconciliations are in.

lb.verdictNote: A verdict is not a label and does not appear on a product card. It is an artefact: a question, the method used to settle it, the answer, and the minority view kept intact. Averaging the dissent away would destroy the only part a reader cannot get from the table.

ladder.name: Fix your data
ladder.what: Complete feed attributes, correct prices, real stock, EANs that match. Every one of these is a ComparoRank input.
ladder.effect: Largest single lever we can measure: shops that closed their feed-attribute gaps moved a median of 6 rank positions and took 23 % more clicks with no spend at all.
ladder.cannot: Nothing to disclaim — this is not promotion, it is the product being correct about you.

ladder.name: Declare your dosing
ladder.what: Amount per serving for your catalogue, or let us photograph it (label verification add-on).
ladder.effect: Unlocks price per gram of active on your listings. A fully declared product converts better than an undeclared one at the same price, because the comparison can be made at all.
ladder.cannot: Declaring a weak dose does not hide it. The number is the number.
ladder.who: Every shop. The add-on only saves you the work.

ladder.name: Earn the delivery labels
ladder.what: Dispatch inside your own cutoff for 90 days. Measured delivery appears at 8 delivered orders per market.
ladder.effect: Measured delivery is the most-read element on a shop card after price. The promise badge (paid, €39/market) only becomes purchasable once the measurement supports it.
ladder.cannot: The badge cannot be bought ahead of the measurement, and the claim rate is published beside it.
ladder.who: Every shop. Eligibility is measured from orders.

ladder.name: Answer people
ladder.what: Reply to reviews, answer Q&A, post announcements, run a shop desk hour in a market room.
ladder.effect: Answers fast is a computed label. Shops that answer above 55 % of reviews hold 0.4 more stars on the same product mix — the same goods, described by calmer customers.
ladder.cannot: A reply cannot remove a review, and staff must post from a verified shop account.
ladder.who: Every shop. Q&A concierge (€69) does the chasing for you.

ladder.name: Shop desk hour
ladder.what: A scheduled, labelled hour in one market room where your staff answer anything. Moderated by the section moderators.
ladder.effect: Small and durable: a desk hour produces a median of 14 answered questions and two promoted topics that keep answering for months.
ladder.cannot: No selling, no links, no price claims we cannot check against your feed. One desk per shop per market per week.

ladder.name: Answer a demand signal
ladder.what: Members pledge what they would pay for a product in their market. You can answer publicly with a price commitment and a window.
ladder.effect: The highest-intent surface we have: a pledge is a shopper telling you their price before you spend anything to find them.
ladder.cannot: A commitment is published as a commitment. Missing it is recorded on your profile like a missed delivery promise.

ladder.name: Run deals
ladder.what: Coupons and price drops in the deal hub and on product pages.
ladder.effect: Deal-hub placement is ordered by community confidence and total price, so a good deal outranks a bigger budget. Extra slots buy volume, not position.
ladder.cannot: Slots do not affect deal ordering. A code that fails gets voted down and drops.
ladder.who: Free plan gets 3 slots; €29 buys 5 more.

ladder.name: Native comparison card
ladder.what: A sponsored card after the organic offer table, with the same columns as an organic row.
ladder.effect: Best-performing paid unit we sell: 4.1 % click rate, because it carries real data rather than a slogan.
ladder.cannot: It sits after the table, never inside it, and it never changes the order of a single organic row.
ladder.who: Any advertiser. Creative checked against your feed.

ladder.name: Category or market featured card
ladder.what: A labelled card in the rail of a category page or market hub, targeted to markets you actually ship to.
ladder.effect: Reach at the point of category intent. We check the lane before the creative goes live — a shop that cannot ship there cannot advertise there.
ladder.cannot: One sponsored unit per surface per session, capped at 12 % of the visible area.

ladder.name: Homepage featured
ladder.what: Featured shop or featured deal on the homepage, labelled, two and three slots respectively.
ladder.effect: Largest single audience on the site. Brand recall rather than conversion — the click rate is half the native card’s.
ladder.cannot: Cannot appear as an offer row, cannot carry a best-value claim, cannot be targeted at a named person.

ladder.name: Market launch package
ladder.what: Six weeks across the market hub, a category card, a newsletter slot and a market-digest mention.
ladder.effect: Built for a shop entering one of the 27 markets from zero. Includes the onboarding work, not just the inventory.
ladder.cannot: Capped at one package per market per quarter, so a market cannot be bought outright.
ladder.who: Growth and above, or a brand with a market launch.

affiliateRules: Our redirect log is the record. When a network and our log disagree we publish both figures and reconcile, rather than quietly taking the higher one.
A click we cannot attribute is not billed to anyone. Unattributed clicks are reported as unattributed.
Commission never touches ComparoRank. The rank inputs are price, availability, trust, delivery and data quality — the commission field is not read by the ranking code at all.

juryRules: Up to nine members are drawn and a majority of the seated panel decides. The draw is seeded from the case id, so it is reproducible and auditable after the fact — and the seat count follows the eligible pool rather than an aspiration, so it shrinks when the pool does.

The verdict, the tally and every reason are public. The evidence is public unless it contains an order number or an address.
One appeal, to a fresh panel of nine, none of whom sat on the first. The second verdict stands.
Comparo may remove illegal content without a panel, and must log it publicly within 24 hours with the legal basis.
Panel service earns 120 XP. It cannot be bought, and it is not visible to shops.

returnsRules: The index counts fault, not volume. A shop with many changed-mind returns and no errors scores better than one with few returns that were all wrong items.
Damaged in transit counts half: the carrier shares it, the packaging does not.
Duplicate orders are not counted at all.
Below eight delivered orders in a market nothing is published — the same threshold the delivery figures use.
Fault needs three returns before it is scored. Below that a pair is scored on refund speed alone: one return says nothing about a shop’s error rate and everything about how fast it pays.
Refund time is measured from the day the return was logged, not from the day the shop chose to process it.
Who pays the return postage is published as a fact, not scored. A shop that charges for returns and says so is not being dishonest.

returnsActions.label: Publish a longer window
returnsActions.effect: Return window is on the profile and in the comparison. 30 days converts measurably better than 14.

returnsActions.label: Pay return postage
returnsActions.effect: Published as a fact beside the window. The strongest single signal in this block.

returnsActions.label: Refund SLA add-on
returnsActions.effect: We chase your return queue and escalate anything past your stated window; median refund time is published either way.

returnsActions.label: Fix packaging
returnsActions.effect: Damaged-in-transit is the one return reason a shop can engineer away. It counts half, and it is half of most bad indices.

knowledgeBase.title: Plan and pricing policy
knowledgeBase.body: List prices are public. Discounts above 15 % need Commercial Admin approval and a stated reason in the audit log.

knowledgeBase.title: Discount policy
knowledgeBase.body: Percent discounts cap at 24 months. Trial extensions cap at 14 days. Never discount in exchange for ranking, reviews or trust changes.

knowledgeBase.title: Campaign inventory
knowledgeBase.body: Capacity per placement per market is fixed. Overbooking is refused by the inventory check, not resolved by an opaque auction.

knowledgeBase.title: Affiliate agreements
knowledgeBase.body: CPS is preferred. Rate changes are recorded with the effective date so historical commission stays reconcilable.

knowledgeBase.title: Renewal playbook
knowledgeBase.body: Open with the ROI report, resolve open feed or invoice issues first, then discuss plan fit. Never lead with a discount.

cx.feedIntervalNote: Import interval is an entitlement, not a promise in copy: Free reads your feed daily, Pro every 6 hours, Growth every 3, Enterprise hourly, and the hourly add-on lifts any plan to 1.

addons.name: Delivery promise
addons.why: Publish an enforceable delivery window in one more market, with the claim process behind it.
addons.gate: Eligibility is measured, not bought: 8 delivered orders in that market, 92 % on-time, and a p90 inside the window you want to promise.
addons.cancel: Cancel any time; the badge stays live until the end of the paid month and open claims are still honoured.

addons.name: Delivery promise 48 h
addons.why: A two-day promise in a market where your measured p90 already clears it.
addons.gate: 95 % on-time, p90 ≤ 2.0 days, dispute rate under 2 %, and a deposit that covers 90 days of expected claims.
addons.cancel: Cancel any time; deposit is returned 60 days after the last promised order is delivered.

addons.name: Hourly feed import
addons.why: Your prices go stale the moment you change them. Hourly import is the difference between a correct offer row and a buyer complaint.
addons.gate: Feed must pass validation on 95 % of imports — we will not poll a broken feed more often.

addons.name: Stock webhook
addons.why: Push stock changes as they happen. Out-of-stock clicks are the fastest way to lose a buyer who trusted the listing.
addons.gate: Endpoint must answer our signed test call.

addons.name: Analytics history to 365 days
addons.why: A year of your own price position, clicks and review trend — enough to see a season.
addons.cancel: Monthly. History is retained regardless; the add-on only opens the window.

addons.name: Competitor price alerts
addons.why: Instant notice when a named competitor undercuts you on a shared product, with the offer record attached.
addons.gate: Only shops that list the same product. We do not sell watchlists of shops you do not compete with.

addons.name: Review invitations
addons.why: We invite buyers we can verify, after delivery, once. Verified reviews carry full weight in the average — unverified ones do not.
addons.gate: Invitations are sent by us, to buyers of orders we can match. You never see an address, and you cannot choose who is asked.
addons.cancel: Monthly. Reviews already collected stay published.

addons.name: Q&A concierge
addons.why: Unanswered buyer questions on your profile get chased, escalated at 24 hours and summarised weekly.

addons.name: Label verification
addons.why: We photograph and verify amount-per-serving for your catalogue, so your listings can be compared on price per gram of active instead of price per tub.
addons.gate: We publish what the panel says, including when it disagrees with your feed. That is the point of it.
addons.cancel: Monthly. Verified dosing records stay published.

addons.name: Market pack
addons.why: Localised profile, market analytics, market price position and campaign booking in one region.
addons.gate: Listing and ComparoRank position are free in all 27 markets and are not part of this. A pack buys work, not placement.

addons.name: Extra deal slots
addons.why: Run five more coupons or price drops at once.
addons.gate: Slots do not affect deal ranking; the deal hub orders by confidence and total price.

addons.name: Campaign inventory share
addons.why: Reserve more of the sponsored inventory in the markets you sell in.
addons.gate: Sponsored inventory is capped per surface and always labelled. A larger share never changes organic order.
addons.cancel: Monthly; booked campaigns run to their end date.

addons.name: Extra team seats
addons.why: Three more people with their own login and audit trail.

addons.name: Support SLA 4 h
addons.why: Four working hours to first human response, on data disputes as well as billing.

cx.addonNote: Add-ons are priced work. None of them can be bought: ComparoRank position, review weight or visibility, a trust badge, a delivery promise you have not measured up to, or a place in an editorial comparison.

cx.revenueMixNote: Six lines, and the interesting thing is not their order — it is that none of them can buy a ranking position, a review weight or a trust badge. Buyer subscriptions are large because members outnumber shops by three orders of magnitude, not because the comparison is gated: a free account sees exactly the same offer table in exactly the same order.

gp.what: A delivery promise is a shop’s commitment to a delivery window, published by us only when our own order records show the shop already meets it, and backed by a deposit the shop puts up in advance.
gp.whatNot: We are not the seller. We never hold the price of the goods, we cannot refund a purchase, and we do not insure the parcel. What the guarantee covers is the promise we published: if the window is missed, the buyer gets the shipping paid back from the shop’s deposit and the miss is counted publicly against the shop.

process.detail: Open the order on Comparo and press "parcel was late". Nothing to write — we already hold the promise, the dispatch and the delivery date.
The promised window, the carrier events and the delivery date are compared automatically. Most claims resolve without a human.
The shop sees the same record and can contest with carrier evidence. Buyer-caused delays are the usual successful contest.
Shipping is returned to your card by the shop, or from the deposit if the shop does not act. The miss is counted on the public shop page either way.

buyerSide: You do not need a paid account to claim. The guarantee belongs to the promise, not to a subscription.
Plus files and chases it for you, which matters only if the shop contests.
A claim never affects your standing, your points or your ability to review.
We publish the claim rate per shop per market whether the shop likes it or not.
